ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct risk-based screening before incorporation, banking, ownership changes, and material payments. Screen all natural-person UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, intermediaries, major suppliers, customers, and counterparties against United Nations Security Council sanctions, European Union sanctions, Spanish domestic sanctions and terrorism-financing lists, and OFAC lists where a US nexus exists or as a risk-control measure. Identify domestic and foreign PEPs, family members, and known close associates; obtain senior-management approval, establish source of wealth and source of funds, apply enhanced ongoing monitoring, and document false-positive resolution. For recombinant insulin manufacturing, apply enhanced controls to government tenders, sovereign health letters of credit, distributors, customs intermediaries, and payments involving high-risk jurisdictions. File suspicious transaction reports with SEPBLAC where legally required and do not disclose the filing to the subject.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) online denomination-certification service: https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be distinct from existing registered or reserved names and must include the legal-form designation or accepted abbreviation, such as Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, S.L., or S.R.L. Names may be in Spanish or another language, provided they comply with public-order, distinctiveness, and registry rules. Local-script or transliterated names are not generally mandatory, but the proposed name must be capable of registration in the Spanish Commercial Registry. The name certificate is required for incorporation before a Spanish notary.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Royal, Crown, Kingdom, or equivalent official references
Bank, banking, credit, finance, insurance, securities, stock exchange, or equivalent regulated-financial terms
Official institutional, governmental, military, diplomatic, or public-authority references
Terms implying a public body, public-interest status, professional qualification, or regulated activity without authorization
Names contrary to law, public order, morality, or public decency
Names confusingly similar to existing registered or reserved corporate names
Geographical, international, or sector-specific terms whose use could mislead the public or require prior regulatory authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit the proposed names in ranked order through the RMC denomination-certification service, normally with up to five alternatives. A favorable certificate is generally valid for three months for incorporation; the name is maintained in the registry reservation system for up to six months, subject to the applicable Commercial Registry Regulations. If rejected, obtain the written grounds, compare the proposal against the RMC name-distinctiveness and prohibited-term rules, and either submit a corrected application or file the applicable governmental appeal against the registrar's decision before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública through the relevant Commercial Registry, normally within one month from notification where the applicable administrative appeal period is one month. Preserve filing evidence, certified translations, and proof of authority. A rejection does not authorize use of the name in contracts, marketing, banking, or regulatory applications.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish Sociedad Limitada must have a registered office in Spain corresponding to the place of effective management or the principal establishment or operation, subject to Companies Act requirements. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for the registered-office function of a holding or administrative company if it provides reliable legal-notice handling, books, records, and access for authorities. It is not sufficient as operational substance for recombinant human insulin manufacturing. Manufacturing requires an appropriately licensed and inspected facility, qualified personnel, quality systems, batch and pharmacovigilance records, storage and distribution controls, and compliance with AEMPS, EU pharmaceutical, GMP, environmental, occupational-safety, and potentially regional-authority requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High. No universal statutory probability is published. For an insulin manufacturing project, an estimated 15%-30% annual probability of a material regulatory, tax, customs, AML, or workplace inspection is a planning estimate rather than a legal statistic; the probability is materially higher before or during manufacturing authorization, GMP certification, product authorization, inspection-triggered investigations, government procurement, adverse-event reporting, or risk-based enforcement.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, 'LSC') — Arts. 19, 20, 22–28 and 62 (S.L. minimum capital €3,000); Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996); Ley 14/2013 de apoyo a los emprendedores (fast-track incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name certification) and the Provincial Commercial Registry of the registered office (Colegio de Registradores de España).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarized public deed of incorporation) followed by mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation. The capital contribution must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Spanish credit institution and the corresponding deposit certificate (certificado de depósito) must be presented to the notary; funds are released to the company only upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — [COMPANY], S.L. Upon unanimous vote of the Sole Director, resolved: 1. Ratify the subscription of 3,000 shares, nominal value €1.00 each, fully paid by the founding partners through the blocked escrow deposit, and confirm the capital of €3,000 as set in the deed. 2. Adopt the registered office at the address described in the deed and authorize execution of the lease and constitution of the company over the operational facility. 3. Appoint [Name] as Sole Administrator with unrestricted corporate, banking, and tax representation powers. 4. Instruct management to complete registration before the Registro Mercantil, obtain the definitive NIF, enrol with Seguridad Social, and apply to AEMPS for the pharmaceutical manufacturing authorization and environmental permits. 5. Approve the company banking arrangements and certify these minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Certification (Negative Certificate of Denomination)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central — online submission via the Colegio de Registradores portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an electronic application for the 'certificación negativa de denominación' selecting up to three alternative corporate names. The registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar denomination is already registered. The certificate confirms exclusive reservation of the approved name for the company for a statutory holding period pending notarization.
required_dossiers: Modelo de solicitud de certificación de denominación social (official form)
List of three proposed corporate names in Spanish
Copy of NIE or passport of each founding member (or legal representative)
Power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned with a positive (conflict) finding, immediately file a fresh application with three alternative names and pay the re-issue fee; the previous reservation may be re-applied only after expiry or express waiver.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Escrow Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (commercial bank) — the designated notary coordinates the deposit validation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the company 'S.L. en constitución' and deposit the EUR 3,000 minimum capital in cash. Obtain a 'certificado de depósito' from the bank indicating the depositor, amount, and blocking restriction; this certificate must name the future company and be dated prior to execution of the deed.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening forms and AML/KYC questionnaire
Preliminary draft of the deed and bylaws
NIE/passport copies of all subscribers
Corporate name certificate (reservation)
Statement of source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires correction of the account title or the deposit is short of EUR 3,000, the difference must be topped up or a supplementary deposit made, and a new certificate issued before the notarial appointment; the notary will reject the deed without a compliant certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Spanish Public Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notaría — fedatario público) designated by the founders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders execute the 'escritura pública de constitución' before a notary. The deed must include the corporate name, object (manufacture of pharmaceutical preparations, ISIC 2100/recombinant insulin), registered office, capital structure, bylaws, administration structure and appointment of the Sole Administrator. The notary issues the 'primera copia' for Commercial Registry filing, and also reports the deed to the AEAT and the Commercial Registry in accordance with Law 10/2010.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate issued by Registro Mercantil Central
Bank deposit certificate for EUR 3,000
Draft bylaws (Estatutos Sociales)
NIE/passport certificates of all founding partners
Bank statement confirming the escrow balance
Identificación fiscal documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues an 'acta de manifestaciones' or withholds execution due to missing documentation, the defect is cured by filing the missing certificate and reserving a new notarial appointment; formal errors in the draft deed are corrected before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provisional NIF (CIF) Application with the Tax Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — applicable Provincial Tax Office (Delegación de la AEAT).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 (Declaración censal) together with the 'primera copia' of the deed to obtain the provisional corporate tax identification number (CIF/NIF) within the statutory deadline following notarization. The provisional NIF authorizes the company to carry out all preparatory acts, including the registry filing and bank account finalization.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 (census declaration, duly signed)
Primera copia (first copy) of the notarial deed
NIE/DNI of the Sole Administrator
Power of attorney of signatory, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT issues a query requiring additional evidence, resubmit within the prescribed term; if the form is rejected for formal defects, file a corrected Modelo 036 and schedule an in-person appointment (cita previa) to expedite the provisional NIF.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration (Inscripción en el Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil corresponding to the registered office of the S.L.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the 'primera copia' of the deed to the Provincial Commercial Registry within two months after notarization. The registrar performs legal qualification (calificación) and, upon approval, issues the certificate of registration that perfects the legal personality of the company. The registry fee is calculated according to the issued capital.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed of incorporation
Provisional NIF certificate (Form 036 acceptance)
Original negative name certificate
NIE/DNI of the appointed administrator
Receipt of payment of AJD (Documentos Notariales) tax, if applicable
Registry filing fee payment order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a negative calificación, cure the noted defects within the two-month filing period and resubmit. If the registry denies inscription, appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within the statutory timeframe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF, IAE Registration and Electronic Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Provincial Tax Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, present the Commercial Registry certificate of inscription to the AEAT and file an updated Modelo 036 to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive CIF/NIF. Simultaneously register the company in the IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) under code 2100 (pharmaceutical manufacturing) and, if applicable, in the VAT register. Obtain the digital certificate (certificado digital) for all electronic filings and electronic invoicing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by the Registro Mercantil
Updated Modelo 036 (census statement with definitive NIF request)
Certified copy of the public deed
NIE/DNI of the Sole Administrator
Proof of registered office and IAE economic activity code
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is withheld because of pending registry data, resolve the registry qualification first; book a cita previa at the AEAT to expedite the issuance. Errors in IAE classification are corrected by filing a supplementary declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) — Provincial Directorate of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the employer registration application (Modelo TA.6) to obtain the employer contribution account code (código de cuenta de cotización, CCC). This is mandatory before hiring staff and for enrolling the Sole Administrator in the appropriate social security regime. The company also begins the occupational risk prevention scheme with a qualified prevention service.
required_dossiers: Modelo TA.6 (employer registration form)
Definitive NIF certificate
Certified copy of the deed of incorporation
Certificate of Commercial Registry inscription
NIE/DNI of the Sole Administrator
Copy of the constitution of the prevention service (external SPA contract)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TGSS returns the application for inconsistency, resubmit the corrected TA.6 within the granted period; retroactive employer registration may be requested from the date the conditions were met, subject to payment of any resulting contributions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Activity License and Opening/Operating License (Licencia de Actividad y Apertura)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento of the municipality where the registered office and industrial facility are located — Department of Urbanism and Economic Activities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a certified technical project (proyecto técnico) prepared by a competent architect/engineer, together with the environmental, fire safety and urban-compatibility declarations. The license is classified as a conditioned industrial activity ('calificada') and requires municipal administrative review and, in some municipalities, a public hearing. Upon approval, the municipality issues the 'licencia de apertura' before the start of operations.
required_dossiers: Certified technical project and architectural plans
Fire safety project and certificate of compliance (RD 513/2017, CTE DB-SI)
Wastewater discharge application to municipal sewer operator
Environmental impact/emissions declaration for the industrial installation
Municipal fee payment receipts
Report of site inspection by municipal technicians
Proof of public hearing notification, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues a negative report, correct the technical deficiencies and resubmit. In the event of administrative silence exceeding the legal term, the company may request a certificate of tacit authorization where the applicable municipal ordinance permits, or file an administrative appeal before the administrative courts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS) — Ministerio de Sanidad (Spanish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency, Ministry of Health).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización de Fabricación de Medicamentos de Uso Humano (Manufacturing Authorization under Royal Decree 824/2010, certifying GMP compliance for the recombinant human insulin production facility).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental — Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO), acting with the competent regional environmental body for the facility's location.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA — Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Ordinaria) under Ley 21/2013, Annex I Group 10 (pharmaceutical/chemical installations); additionally, the facility requires an Integrated Environmental Authorization (Autorización Ambiental Integrada — AAI) under Ley 16/2002 (IPPC).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with Real Decreto 817/2015 (environmental quality standards), BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L prior to discharge; VOCs: compliance with Real Decreto 815/2013 and EU Directive 2010/75/EU emission limit values for pharmaceutical operations; waste: management under Ley 7/2022 with mandatory hazardous waste producer registration (ISIC/NAICS 2100/325414) and full traceability of organic solvent and pharmaceutical residues.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory municipal fire safety certificate based on approved Fire Protection Project (RD 513/2017 and CTE DB-SI); structural load inspection certificate signed by a competent architect/technical architect covering the GMP cleanroom floors and anti-vibration systems; occupational health and safety clearance including a workplace risk prevention plan and health surveillance program run by an accredited external Prevention Service (SPA), plus the pre-operational inspection (acta de comprobación) by the regional health authority prior to the first GMP batch production.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the Central Registry, Delegación Central de Grandes Contribuyentes, and Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales; official portal www.agenciatributaria.es; coordination with the Registro Mercantil Central for corporate legal registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An inbound foreign-owned SL obtains its NIF (CIF-equivalent) through a Spanish notary: (1) obtain the negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social) from the Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute the incorporation deed before a notary; (3) the notary requests the provisional NIF electronically from the AEAT Central Registry (issued instantly, valid 6 months); (4) file the deed at the provincial Mercantile Registry within 2 months (usual completion 4-8 weeks); (5) request the definitive NIF immediately after Mercantile Registry registration (issued electronically, same day). Parallel obligations: register in the Censo de Empresarios before commencing activity (modelo 036/037); obtain an EORI number for customs and export operations; each non-resident shareholder must obtain a Spanish NIF through a legal representative with power of attorney. The definitive NIF is the sole taxpayer identifier for corporate income tax (IS), VAT/IVA, and customs procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an SL incorporated and registered in Spain is a Spanish tax resident subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) on worldwide income at the general 25% rate, or 15% for a newly created SL in the first two years with a positive taxable base (art. 29.1 LIS 27/2014). No pass-through or check-the-box classification is available under Spanish law. Dividend/participation exemption applies under art. 21 LIS for qualifying holdings. The Canary Islands ZEC special 4% rate is available only in the Canary Islands territorial scope, which does not cover a Peninsular biopharma export platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no US-style check-the-box election. Available elections: (i) consolidated tax group regime (régimen de grupos de sociedades) for direct or indirect shareholding of at least 75% (70% for listed groups) held for more than one full tax year, with irrevocable entry for a 3-year period; (ii) reinvestment relief (deducción por reinversión) and equalization reserve (reserva de nivelación) for entities with turnover up to 10,000,000 EUR; (iii) hybrid mismatch adjustments under arts. 15 ter-15 quinquies LIS implementing ATAD 2 — mandatory, not elective; (iv) patent box (art. 23 LIS): 60% reduction on qualifying intangible income, subject to substance and tracing rules — relevant for process IP in recombinant insulin manufacturing; (v) VAT optional cash-basis regime (régimen especial de criterio de caja) for turnover up to 2,000,000 EUR, irrevocable for 3 years — usually unattractive for exporters; (vi) SME VAT exemption under EU Directive 2020/285 with an 85,000 EUR annual turnover cap on domestic supplies, exercisable by notification in the Censo de Empresarios since 1 January 2024 — generally inadvisable for a biopharma exporter because input VAT deduction is lost; (vii) OSS/non-established taxable person registration for intra-community distance sales (10,000 EUR threshold).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA), governed by Ley 37/1992 and RD 1624/1992, harmonized with Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis turnover threshold: any person carrying out a business activity in Spanish territory must register in the Censo de Empresarios before commencing operations (modelo 036/037). The special SME exemption introduced under EU Directive 2020/285 applies only when annual turnover does not exceed 85,000 EUR for domestic supplies and 10,000 EUR for intra-community distance sales; it must be exercised via the Censo and is not suitable for an exporter with significant recoverable input VAT. A pharmaceutical manufacturer exporting recombinant human insulin must register for VAT regardless of turnover in order to obtain the export exemption and process VAT refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: (1) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información, RD 596/2016, operative since 1 July 2017): mandatory for large enterprises with turnover above 6,000,000 EUR, VAT groups, and taxpayers in certain special regimes; requires near-real-time submission of issued/received invoice records to AEAT within 4 working days of the accounting entry date, with 8 working days for taxpayers filing annual returns; (2) Verifactu (Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece', art. 12; RD 1007/2023): mandatory integrity and traceability system for all invoice-issuing software; software producers must be compliant by 31 December 2024 and all other taxable persons by 31 December 2025; generates QR-coded, hash-chain-protected electronic invoice records (XML) that must be made available to AEAT on request — not a per-transaction clearance system but an audit-ready fiscal memory; (3) Export customs clearance: electronic filing of the DUA through the AEAT customs window ('Aduanas 24/7' system using TARIC/DEA), with EORI validation required; the SII export book entries must reference the DUA and the date of physical departure; (4) mandatory e-invoicing in B2G relations (Facturae standard is already operational) and future general B2B e-invoicing obligations under Ley 18/2022 are expected to be fully enforced in 2026; SII and Verifactu already provide the functional equivalent for tax control purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The full export exemption (exención plena con derecho a deducción) under art. 21.1 Ley 37/1992 applies when goods are dispatched or transported by the seller or a third party on the seller's behalf from Spain/EU territory to a destination outside the EU (excluding the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla). The goods must physically leave EU territory within 3 months from the date of dispatch (art. 21.5 Ley 37/1992). This 0% rate covers exports of recombinant human insulin to sovereign health programs in Latin America using letter-of-credit rails, provided the exporter is VAT-registered in Spain and holds a valid EORI number. Directly ancillary transport, loading, and handling services (arts. 21.18-21.22 Ley 37/1992) are also exempt; separately invoiced insurance and disbursements follow general place-of-supply rules. Input VAT on raw materials, utilities, logistics, and quality-control services used for the exported insulin is fully creditable through the monthly model 303/390 cycle, with refunds processed through the SII-audited route; no special prior export-refund authorization is required beyond standard registration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo), including the electronic exit confirmation (certificado de salida) generated by the Spanish customs system (TARIC/DEA)

Bill of Lading (B/L) for sea freight, Air Waybill (AWB) for air freight, or CMR with electronic customs exit validation for road transport, evidencing departure from Spain/EU to the non-EU destination

Commercial invoice stating the Spanish exporter's NIF-VAT and EORI, the foreign purchaser's full details, the recombinant human insulin batch reference, Incoterms (FOB/CIF/EXW), and explicit reference to the art. 21 LIVA export exemption
Packing list and, where applicable, the EMA/AEMPS batch-release certificate and certificate of analysis for biologics/pharmaceuticals
Payment evidence: SWIFT MT103 or a bank letter-of-credit credit advice under the Sovereign_Health_LC rail, cross-referenced to the invoice number and the export declaration
EUR.1 / EUR-MED certificate or REX invoice origin declaration when a preferential origin claim is made in the importing country (non-constitutive for Spanish zero-rating)
Freight forwarder instructions and transport operator booking confirmations, retained by the exporter for at least 5 years
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT central risk units (ONIF and Customs) target exporters on red flags such as rapid growth of zero-rated exports to high-risk jurisdictions, persistent VAT refund claims without matching production capacity, SII discrepancies between export books and the DUA register, and irregular LC documentation. If the export exemption is denied (goods never left the EU, export completed after the 3-month deadline, or falsified documents), AEAT will: (i) regularize the transaction and assess the omitted output VAT (21% standard rate, or 4% super-reduced rate if recharacterized as a domestic supply of human-use medicines); (ii) disallow input VAT deductions when underlying records are not substantiated; (iii) charge statutory late-payment interest on tax debt (5.55% per annum in 2025); (iv) impose penalties under arts. 191-193 Ley 58/2003 — for an infracción grave, a penalty of 50%-150% of the omitted amount (100%-150% when false documentation is used), plus enforcement surcharges of 5%-20% in the apremio phase. Where the amount defrauded exceeds 120,000 EUR, criminal prosecution under art. 305 Código Penal may follow (1-5 years imprisonment and a fine of 2-6 times the defrauded amount), together with corporate criminal liability for the SL under art. 310 bis CP. The statute of limitation is 4 years from the end of the voluntary filing period (arts. 66-67 LGT); the exporter bears the burden of proving physical exit from the EU and must preserve the full documentation bundle for at least 5 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and supervised by the European Central Bank for prudential purposes; foreign-exchange and international-investment statistical control is coordinated with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOMER) within the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Commerce and Business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is an euro-area Member State with full capital and current account convertibility under Article 63 TFEU and the Spanish Law on Foreign Investment and its implementing regulations. The euro is freely convertible; no general central-bank approval is required for inward capital contributions, dividend remittances, royalty payments, or repayment of foreign loans. The remaining controls are limited to statistical declarations and balance-of-payments reporting for transactions exceeding EUR 50,000, EU/UN/OFAC sanctions compliance, AML/CFT controls, foreign-investment screening for critical sectors under Royal Decree-Law 8/2020, and non-resident income tax (IRNR) compliance on distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no forced repatriation deadline for export proceeds in Spain. Export collections may be held in EUR or foreign currency accounts in Spanish banks or abroad. For balance-of-payments statistics, export receipts equal to or greater than EUR 50,000 must be reported to Banco de España through the Spanish reporting bank on the relevant periodic declaration; the exporter must retain underlying invoices, customs declarations (DUA), transport documents, and proof of receipt. The practical statutory timeline is the reporting period applicable to each bank's balance-of-payments return, generally monthly or quarterly, rather than a same-day surrender deadline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium/Low as exclusive treasury bank; High as a supplemental SEPA collection and payment gateway. A fintech EMI authorised under PSD2 and passported into Spain may be registered with Banco de España and can lawfully execute payments, FX conversion, and e-money transactions, but it remains a payment institution rather than a credit institution, so it cannot accept repayable deposits, hold client funds as a core commercial banking service, issue documentary credits, or open a capital-escrow account in the manner of a full Spanish bank. Offshore EMIs outside the EEA face additional legal constraints under Spanish AML law and are generally not acceptable as the primary treasury cloud for a high-risk pharmaceutical manufacturer; if used at all, they should be limited to non-core subthreshold payments through a supervised EU licensee with a letter of no-objection from Banco de España.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish Law 10/2010 on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing does not prescribe an absolute physical interview for corporate account opening. Remote onboarding is legally available where directors are identified through a bank-approved video call with eIDAS qualified electronic signatures or official identity documents and where the bank's risk-based approach accepts that method. However, for a high-risk pharma/Biopharma licence with non-resident shareholders (ISIC 2100), most tier-1 Spanish banks will require at least one physical compliance interview of a signatory or UBO in Madrid/Barcelona, notarised and apostilled company documents, a certified UBO register extract (Registro de Titularidades Reales), and evidence of physical substance in Spain. Remote opening is possible in practice only after a bank-specific EDD clearance and with a Spanish corporate proxy or locally resident professional fiduciary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Applicant is a newly formed Spanish SL in GMP pharmaceutical manufacturing with non-EU shareholding and no local operating track record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Registro Mercantil certificate, AEMPS manufacturing or import authorisation for insulin products, lease or ownership of physical premises, payroll and substance documentation, audited opening balance sheet, board resolution appointing local management, detailed business plan, and licences for the target ISIC scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain includes offshore companies, trusts, or foundations in an opaque jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish UBO certificate, corporate structure chart with ownership percentages, notarised trust deed or foundation deed, source-of-wealth statement, independent legal opinion on beneficial ownership, and confirmations of the economic purpose of each entity in the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection appears as a rapid movement of funds from a partner in a higher-risk Latin American jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Origin-bank account statements, notarised capital increase deed, share-subscription agreement, source-of-funds declaration, audited financial statements or tax returns of the transferor, and a documented commercial rationale for the investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade collections and documentary letter of credit flows involve high-risk pharmaceutical/TBML exposure with intermediaries in third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original supply/purchase contracts, UCP600-compliant LC documents, commercial invoices, duty-paid customs declarations (DUA), bills of lading or airway bills, inspection certificates, warehouse receipts, and identity/UBO records of the trade counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name-based sanctions or PEP screening generates a hit due to shared names with politically exposed persons or listed entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clean-screen adjudication memo, identity document verification, confirmation of nationality and residency, enhanced due diligence questionnaire, negative news research, sanctions-screening report, and sign-off from the AML compliance officer and where necessary the board risk committee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity must be wired via SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV to a Spanish-based account using the beneficiary IBAN (ES checksum + 20 digits) and BIC, with field 70 stating the ISO 20022 purpose code accepted by the receiving bank (e.g., EQUI for equity contribution, INTC for intra-group funding) and referencing the notarised capital increase deed. The same wire should be supported by the Spanish public deed elevating capital, registration in the Mercantile Registry, Banco de España balance-of-payments declaration where applicable, and, if the investor is non-EU in the health/pharma/critical sector, a prior-authorisation assessment under Royal Decree-Law 8/2020. The receiving bank will verify the corporate signatories, UBO registry, tax ID (CIF/NIF), and the economic substance evidence before releasing funds to the fully operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use TARGET2 for high-value euro settlement, SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for euro payments to EU/EEA beneficiaries, and SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV for all non-euro or non-EEA payments. For commercial trade contracts with Latin American buyers/suppliers, open or receive letters of credit through SWIFT MT700/MT707 under UCP600, advise negotiation/acceptance via MT754/MT756, and settle reimbursements through the issuing bank's correspondent rail or Eurosystem TARGET2 account. Additional clearing options include bank-hosted trade finance portals, SWIFT GPI real-time payment tracking, and escrow-backed LC disbursements where sovereign health procurement requires definitive security.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Outright FX Forward (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and liquid LATAM EMFX pairs) under an ISDA/FBF Master Agreement
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for illiquid or restricted Latin American currencies such as the Argentine peso, with cash settlement in EUR/USD
FX Swap (simultaneous spot and forward exchange) for efficient short-term funding of working capital
Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) with exchange of principal and interest for medium-term balance-sheet hedging of USD/LATAM debt or receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days after the six month period following fiscal year end; for calendar-year entities, due by 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges: 5% (immediate), 10% (up to 3 months), 15% (3-6 months), 20% (over 6 months) of tax due; late-payment interest; penalties up to 150% of the omission

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by shareholders' meeting; meeting must be held within six months of fiscal year end (i.e., by 31 July for calendar-year SL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cierre registral (company locked from filing registry documents); administrative fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000; director liability for damages

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 1 March of the year following the calendar year of reportable transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of EUR 300 to EUR 20,000 per omitted or incorrect data item, scaled by the volume of transactions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Activity Tax (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas, IAE) — Annual Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AEAT in coordination with municipal tax offices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return (Modelo 848) from 1 to 20 November; payment period for quota liabilities begins 1 September and ends 15 November (or 20 November if by direct debit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 5% to 20% for late payment; late-payment interest; coercive collection procedure; penalty for non-taxation up to 150% of omitted amount

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (through the Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneous with the annual accounts deposit; by 31 July for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company closure (cierre registral) for non-compliance; fines of up to EUR 60,000; civil and criminal liability for directors

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit required if an SL meets at least two of the following thresholds in two consecutive years: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 2,851,000; net annual turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000; average employees exceeding 50. Audit also required for entities belonging to a consolidated group or having listed debt securities
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC), aligned with EU-endorsed IFRS; large companies may opt for IFRS-EU for individual accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SL must maintain an internal Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Libro Registro de Titulares Reales) and update it within 10 days of any shareholding or control change. Annual confirmation is effected through the Depósito de Cuentas Anuales, reporting any modifications to UBO data; failure to update or confirm triggers registral closure and administrative penalties
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for new entities in first two years with positive taxable base; R&D tax credits up to 25% of qualifying expenses; patent box regime for IP income at 10% effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) via electronic filing system (Sede Electrónica de la AEAT)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The 25th day following the 6 months after the end of the tax year (e.g., for calendar year-end, by July 25)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report taxable income from Spanish sources, applying arm's length principles and any applicable tax treaty provisions.
Apply the general 25% rate or the reduced 15% rate if eligible as a new entity; otherwise, apply any special regime.
Calculate the gross tax liability before credits and deductions.
Apply R&D tax credits, double taxation relief, and other eligible incentives; ensure documentation is retained.
Final tax due after all credits and deductions; if negative, indicate refund claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings and payments on account (Retenciones y pagos a cuenta)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report any withholdings on income and quarterly installment payments made during the year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 5% of tax due if filed within 3 months of deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, 20% after 12 months, plus late payment interest. Additionally, a fine of €1,000 per data item for incorrect or omitted data.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% (domestic rate for non-residents; 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥5% for 12 months)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, submit Form 112 (Non-Resident Income Tax) and provide a Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) from the recipient's tax authority. The payer must retain the TRC and apply the reduced rate at source, or request a refund if over-withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 19% domestic, 0% under EU Interest and Royalties Directive if conditions met; Royalties: 24% domestic, 0% under EU Directive if conditions met, otherwise treaty rates (e.g., 10% under US-Spain treaty).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €10 million net turnover for Local File; €50 million group consolidated turnover for Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) and requires economic substance for tax residency. The company must have adequate personnel, premises, and functions to support its activities; otherwise, it may be deemed a shell and denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, overstatement of deductions, or use of artificial transactions to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 150% of the tax evaded, plus interest; criminal liability for fraud exceeding €120,000 may lead to imprisonment of 1-6 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; may face civil restitution, travel bans, and disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without real economic substance—no employees, no physical presence, or no actual business activity—used solely to channel funds or avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification as a tax haven entity, denial of treaty benefits, and penalties up to 150% of tax avoided; potential criminal charges for fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for taxes and penalties if they are the de facto managers; may face criminal prosecution and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML procedures—customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting, or record-keeping—especially in high-risk sectors like pharmaceuticals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €5 million or 10% of annual turnover for serious breaches; criminal liability for money laundering with imprisonment up to 6 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for AML failures, including fines and imprisonment if they knowingly or negligently facilitate money laundering.
